newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share trading active after holidays.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share trading active after holidays.

text.p: Trading was robust on the Nigerian stock market on Monday after four days' public holiday to mark the Moslem festival of Eid-El-Kabir, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 8799.95, up from 8789.89 last Wednesday, the last day of trading.
Traders said turnover had risen to near normal levels from the lull that followed the automation of the clearing system a week ago.
"The market is almost back to normal," said one dealer.
Conglomerates and oil shares led trading, propelled by higher demand.
John Holt Nigeria Plc closed higher 9.90 naira as did Lever Brothers Nigeria Plc at 29.80 naira, PZ Industries Plc at 29.75 and UAC Nigeria Plc at 19.90 naira.
Oil companies also moved mostly higher with National Oil Plc at 60.50 naira, Total Nigeria Plc at 60.90 naira and African Petroleum Plc at 58.50 naira.
Lower-priced shares also made gains with footwear Bata Nigeria Plc appreciating at 1.25 naira as did UTC Nigeria Plc at 1.18 naira.
"The market feels these stocks have room to improve," said one dealer.
But banking shares, which have been rising since the beginning of the year when the government demanded they should increase their capital bases ninefold, lost steam in Monday.
Many dropped slightly with First Bank Nigeria Plc at 20.60, UBA Nigeria Plc falling to 15.45 naira and Union Bank Nigeria Plc down at 17.00 naira.
